p.src: Now the Latter Lord in Chengdu heard that Deng Ai had taken Mianzhu and that Zhuge Zhan and his son had perished. Greatly alarmed, he hastily summoned his civil and military officials to deliberate. A close attendant reported, “Outside the city, the people are supporting the old and carrying the young; their cries shake the air as each flees to save his life.” The Latter Lord was terrified and knew not what to do. Suddenly a scout rode in with word that the Wei army was nearing the city walls. The assembled officials said, “Our troops are few and our commanders scarce; we cannot meet the enemy in battle. We should abandon Chengdu at once and flee to the seven commanderies of Nanzhong. The terrain there is rugged and defensible; we may enlist the tribal forces and later return to recover our realm.” Qiao Zhou, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, said, “That must not be done. The southern tribes have long been rebellious, and in ordinary times we have shown them no kindness. If we seek refuge with them now, great calamity will surely befall us.” The other officials then memorialized, “Shu and Wu are allies. Now that the crisis is upon us, we may seek refuge with Wu.” Qiao Zhou remonstrated again, “Since ancient times, no Son of Heaven has lived as a dependent in another state. I judge that Wei can swallow Wu, but Wu cannot swallow Wei. To profess submission to Wu would be one humiliation. If Wu should then be swallowed by Wei and Your Majesty must profess submission to Wei as well, that would be humiliation twice over. Better to surrender directly to Wei than seek refuge with Wu. Wei will surely grant Your Majesty a fief: thus, above, you may preserve the ancestral temples, and below, safeguard the common people. I beg Your Majesty to consider this.” The Latter Lord remained undecided and withdrew into the palace.

p.src: The next day, opinions remained sharply divided. Seeing the urgency of the situation, Qiao Zhou submitted another memorial of remonstrance. The Latter Lord accepted Qiao Zhou’s counsel. Just as he was about to go forth and surrender, a man suddenly emerged from behind a screen and fiercely berated Qiao Zhou: “You rotten scholar who clings cravenly to life! How dare you recklessly debate a matter of such consequence to the state! Since ancient times, when has there ever been a Son of Heaven who surrendered?” The Latter Lord looked and saw that it was his fifth son, Liu Chen, Prince of Beidi. The Latter Lord had seven sons: the eldest, Liu Xuan; the second, Liu Yao; the third, Liu Cong; the fourth, Liu Zan; the fifth, Liu Chen, Prince of Beidi; the sixth, Liu Xun; and the seventh, Liu Qu. Of the seven, only Liu Chen had been intelligent from childhood, with exceptional courage and acuity; all the others were weak and meek. The Latter Lord said to him, “All the great ministers now agree that we should surrender. Are you alone relying on hot-blooded courage and seeking to make the whole city run with blood?” Liu Chen replied, “When the First Emperor was alive, Qiao Zhou never took part in affairs of state. Now he presumes to discuss this great matter and readily utters seditious words. It is utterly unreasonable. I humbly estimate that Chengdu still has tens of thousands of troops. Jiang Wei’s entire army is at Jiange. If he learns that the Wei army has assailed the imperial court, he will surely come to our aid. By attacking from within and without, we may win a complete victory. How can we heed the words of a rotten scholar and lightly cast away the foundation laid by the First Emperor?” The Latter Lord rebuked him: “You are a mere child—what can you know of Heaven’s times?” Liu Chen knocked his head upon the ground and wept: “If our situation is truly hopeless, our strength exhausted, and ruin upon us, then father and sons, sovereign and ministers, should make a last stand with our backs to the city and die together for the state, so that we may face the First Emperor. How can we surrender?” The Latter Lord would not listen. Liu Chen burst into loud weeping and cried, “The First Emperor did not establish this foundation with ease. Now it is to be abandoned in a single day. I would rather die than suffer this disgrace!” The Latter Lord ordered his attendants to thrust Liu Chen out through the palace gates. He then commanded Qiao Zhou to compose a letter of surrender and sent the privately appointed Palace Attendant Zhang Shao and Commandant Escorting the Imperial Son-in-law Deng Liang, together with Qiao Zhou, to carry the imperial seal to Luo City and offer submission.

p.src: At that time, Deng Ai sent several hundred armored cavalrymen each day to scout toward Chengdu. That day, when he saw the flag of surrender raised, Deng Ai was overjoyed. Before long, Zhang Shao and the others arrived, and Deng Ai ordered that they be welcomed in. The three men prostrated themselves below the steps and presented the terms of surrender and the imperial seal. Deng Ai opened the letter of surrender and read it. Delighted, he accepted the imperial seal and treated Zhang Shao, Qiao Zhou, Deng Liang, and the others with great honor. Deng Ai wrote a reply and entrusted it to the three men to carry back to Chengdu, so as to reassure the people. The three took leave of Deng Ai and returned directly to Chengdu. They entered the Latter Lord’s presence, presented the reply, and described in detail how kindly Deng Ai had treated them. The Latter Lord broke the seal and read the letter. Greatly pleased, he immediately sent Grand Coachman Jiang Xian with an edict ordering Jiang Wei to surrender without delay. He also sent Li Hu, a Gentleman of the Secretariat, to deliver the official registers to Deng Ai. In all there were 280,000 households; 940,000 men and women; 102,000 armored soldiers; 40,000 officials; more than 400,000 measures of stored grain; 3,000 catties of gold and silver; and 200,000 bolts each of brocade, figured silk, colored silk, and plain silk. The other articles in the storehouses were too numerous to list in full. The first day of the twelfth month was chosen for the sovereign and his ministers to go forth and surrender.

p.src: Now Jiang Xian, the Grand Coachman, came to Sword Pass and presented himself before Jiang Wei, conveying the Latter Lord’s command and telling him of the surrender. Jiang Wei was so shocked that he could not speak. When the generals under his command heard the news, they were all filled with bitter rage. Gnashing their teeth, glaring fiercely, and bristling with fury, they drew their swords, hacked at the rocks, and cried, “We have fought to the death—why did they surrender before us?” Their wailing could be heard for tens of li. Seeing that the men’s hearts still belonged to Han, Jiang Wei soothed them with kindly words: “Do not be troubled, my generals. I have a plan by which the house of Han may be restored.” The generals asked to hear it. Jiang Wei drew them close and whispered the plan into their ears. Surrender flags were immediately raised throughout Sword Pass, and a messenger was first sent to Zhong Hui’s camp to report that Jiang Wei was coming to surrender with Zhang Yi, Liao Hua, Dong Jue, and the others. Zhong Hui was delighted. He sent men to welcome Jiang Wei into his tent and said, “Boyue, why have you come so late?” With a solemn expression and tears streaming down his face, Jiang Wei replied, “The whole army of the state was entrusted to me. For me to have come to this today is already soon enough.” Zhong Hui thought this remarkable. He descended from his seat, exchanged bows with Jiang Wei, and treated him as an honored guest. Jiang Wei said to Zhong Hui, “I have heard that ever since the campaign in Huainan, not one of your calculations has failed. The present ascendancy of the Sima clan is entirely due to your efforts. That is why I willingly bow my head before you. Had it been Deng Shizai, I would have fought him to the death. How could I ever have surrendered to him?” Zhong Hui then broke an arrow as a pledge and swore brotherhood with Jiang Wei. They became exceedingly close, and he allowed Jiang Wei to retain command of his troops as before. Jiang Wei rejoiced inwardly and sent Jiang Xian back to Chengdu.

p.src: After receiving his new title, Zhong Hui immediately summoned Jiang Wei to consult with him: “Deng Ai’s achievements exceed mine, and he has also been appointed Grand Commandant. Now Duke Sima suspects him of rebellious ambitions and has therefore made Wei Guan army supervisor and commanded me to restrain him. What wise counsel have you, Boyue?” Jiang Wei replied, “I have heard that Deng Ai was born to a lowly station and in his youth tended calves for a farming family. Now, by mere chance, he has followed a narrow path from Yinping, climbing trees and scaling cliffs, and won this great success. It sprang from no brilliant strategy but truly depended upon the abundant fortune of the state. Had you not been locked against me at Sword Pass, how could Deng Ai ever have won such an achievement? Now he wishes to make the ruler of Shu Prince of Fufeng, thereby binding the hearts of the people of Shu closely to himself. His rebellious intent is plain without need of words. Duke of Jin is right to suspect him.” Zhong Hui greatly approved of these words. Jiang Wei continued, “Please dismiss your attendants. I have a secret matter to tell you.” Zhong Hui ordered every attendant to withdraw. Jiang Wei drew a map from his sleeve and handed it to Zhong Hui, saying, “Long ago, when the Martial Marquis first emerged from his thatched cottage, he presented this map to the Former Emperor and said, ‘Yizhou has fertile plains stretching a thousand li, a teeming population, and a wealthy realm; it may serve as the foundation of an imperial enterprise.’ Thus the Former Emperor established his dominion at Chengdu. Now that Deng Ai has reached this place, how could he fail to grow wildly ambitious?” Zhong Hui was overjoyed and pointed to the map, asking about the terrain of its mountains and rivers. Jiang Wei explained each feature in turn. Zhong Hui then asked, “What plan should we use to eliminate Deng Ai?” Jiang Wei replied, “While Duke of Jin remains suspicious of him, you should quickly submit a memorial setting forth the signs of Deng Ai’s rebellion. Duke of Jin will surely order you to attack him, and you may capture him at a single stroke.” Zhong Hui followed his advice. He immediately sent a man to carry a memorial to Luoyang, accusing Deng Ai of wielding power arbitrarily, acting without restraint, and courting the people of Shu, and declaring that he would rebel sooner or later. At this, every civil and military official at court was alarmed. Zhong Hui also had Deng Ai’s memorial intercepted on the road, and, imitating Deng Ai’s handwriting, rewrote it with arrogant expressions so as to substantiate his own accusations.

Duke of Jin will surely order you to attack him, and you may capture him at a single stroke.”

Zhong Hui followed his advice. He immediately sent a man to carry a memorial to Luoyang, accusing Deng Ai of wielding power arbitrarily, acting without restraint, and courting the people of Shu, and declaring that he would rebel sooner or later.
At this, every civil and military official at court was alarmed.
Zhong Hui also had Deng Ai’s memorial intercepted on the road, and, imitating Deng Ai’s handwriting, rewrote it with arrogant expressions so as to substantiate his own accusations.

p.src: When Sima Zhao saw Deng Ai’s memorial, he flew into a rage and immediately sent a man to Zhong Hui’s army, ordering him to arrest Deng Ai. He also sent Jia Chong into Xie Valley with thirty thousand troops, while he himself set out on campaign with the emperor of Wei, Cao Huan, in the imperial carriage. Shao Ti, an assistant clerk of the Western Office, remonstrated: “Zhong Hui has six times as many troops as Deng Ai. He alone is sufficient to arrest Deng Ai. Why must Your Excellency go in person?” Sima Zhao laughed and said, “Have you forgotten what you told me before? You once said that Zhong Hui would certainly rebel in the end. This expedition of mine is not truly for Deng Ai, but for Zhong Hui.” Shao Ti smiled and replied, “I feared Your Excellency might have forgotten, and so I asked. Since this is indeed your intention, you must keep it strictly secret and allow no word to escape.” Sima Zhao agreed and set out at the head of a great army. At the time, Jia Chong likewise suspected Zhong Hui of plotting revolt and secretly informed Sima Zhao. Sima Zhao said, “Since I have dispatched you, do you suppose I suspect you as well? Once we reach Chang’an, everything will become clear.” A spy soon reported to Zhong Hui that Sima Zhao had already reached Chang’an. Alarmed, Zhong Hui summoned Jiang Wei to discuss a plan for arresting Deng Ai. Indeed:
